requirements.evidence: The contract is broadly implemented: `app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:27-60`, `app/Models/Ticket.php:83-122`, `app/Policies/TicketPolicy.php:13-15`, both migrations, enums, exception and factories are present. However `app/Models/Queue.php:11` and `app/Models/Ticket.php:16` use `#[Fillable(...)]` from `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\Fillable`, which is not a Laravel 12 API; the attribute is ignored, leaving `$fillable` empty and the default `$guarded = ['*']` in force, so `Queue::factory()->create()` and `Ticket::create([...])` throw `MassAssignmentException` before any issuance can happen. `Ticket::nextCode` (`app/Models/Ticket.php:83-98`) also reuses the number of a deleted latest ticket and can return an already-used code for out-of-order legacy codes.

conventions.evidence: Good use of an `App\Actions` use case (`app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:27`), a policy for the call (`app/Policies/TicketPolicy.php:13`), generated-style migrations with reversible `down()` methods, factories and CHANGELOG/docs updates. Deviations: the fake `#[Fillable]` attribute instead of the project's `$fillable`/`$guarded` convention (`app/Models/Queue.php:11`, `app/Models/Ticket.php:16`) and docs not fully in sync (`docs/business-rules.md:76` still omits `status` from the mutable fields, and the queue section at line 72 omits `labels_i18n`).

security.evidence: `Ticket::call` authorizes with `Gate::forUser($user)->authorize('call', $this)` before any write (`app/Models/Ticket.php:107-109`), `TicketPolicy::call` checks membership of the ticket's entity (`app/Policies/TicketPolicy.php:13-15`), a negative priority is rejected (`app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:29`), and the migrations/factories set attributes deliberately. This backend-only change has no untrusted client parameters or unescaped output; no exploitable weakness found.

tests.evidence: Pest coverage is broad: `tests/Feature/Queue/IssueTicketTest.php` (defaults, priority/channel, consecutive codes, negative priority, inactive and stale queue, retry), `TicketNextCodeTest.php` (A001, A999 -> A1001, malformed, deletion, per-queue), `TicketCallTest.php` (member/admin/owner/stranger/other entity, double call, stale instance), `TicketWriteOnceTest.php`, and the two schema tests. Gaps: the last-deleted-code case is untested, the retry test does not assert the recomputed code, `calledBy()` is untested, and the whole suite would fail at the model fillable blocker.

simplicity.evidence: Lean, direct implementation: a 61-line `IssueTicket` using `DB::transaction`/`lockForUpdate` and a small retry loop (`app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:27-60`), code allocation in one model hook shared by the factory and action (`app/Models/Ticket.php:42-46`), and no service/repository layer or duplicated logic.

readability.evidence: Small typed methods, docblocks on `nextCode` and `call`, explicit exception messages and clear names (`app/Models/Ticket.php:78-125`, `app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:19-53`); no dead code, debug output or inconsistent style.

scope.evidence: Every changed file serves the task: the two models, enums, exception, policy, action, factories, the two migrations, tests, CHANGELOG and the two required docs; no unrelated refactors or features.

issues.explanation: `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\Fillable` is not a Laravel 12 class, so the attributes are ignored, `$fillable` is empty and `$guarded` stays `['*']`; every factory create and `Ticket::create([...])` therefore throws `MassAssignmentException` and the action, factories and tests cannot run.

`nextCode()` uses the last inserted row, so deleting the newest ticket reuses its number (A001, A002 -> delete A002 -> next A002) and an out-of-order valid code can make it return an existing code (A1000 then A999 -> A1000), which collides on every retry; the task says deletion must not reuse a number, while `docs/business-rules.md:86` silently weakens this to 'does not renumber'.

The docs still say only `called_at` and `called_by` may change after issuance, omitting `status` that the task and implementation allow to move waiting -> called, and the new Queue section at line 72 omits the implemented `labels_i18n` field.

The three chained `toThrow` assertions reuse one model instance; after the first failed update leaves `channel` dirty, the later saves would throw because of that stale dirty field, so the test does not independently prove `queue_id` and `issued_at` are immutable.

The forced collision row is inserted inside the same transaction and rolls back with the attempt, so the retry recomputes the same `A001`; the test proves the loop retried but not that a committed competing code is skipped.

review.summary: The change adds the queues/tickets persistence, enums, models, factories, IssueTicket action, a membership-checked single-call policy and extensive Pest coverage, with the required docs and CHANGELOG updates. It cannot be merged as is: both models use a non-existent `#[Fillable]` attribute, leaving mass assignment fully guarded, so every factory/action write and the test suite fail; there are also minor nextCode deletion/out-of-order edge cases and docs gaps.
